newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bishops condemn Larry Flynt film poster.
newsitem.headline: Polish bishops condemn Larry Flynt film poster.

text.p: Polish Roman Catholic bishops have condemned as criminal and sacrilegious a poster advertising the Hollywood film "The People Vs Larry Flynt," which depicts a man in a crucifixion pose on a woman's pelvis.

Cardinal Jozef Macharski earlier this week asked the local prosecutor's office in the southern city of Krakow to investigate whether the distribution of the poster was a criminal act, newspapers reported.

"Contents of this poster offend religious feelings and are against the freedom of conscience and religion, which violates articles...of the criminal code," Macharski said in a letter published in Polish daily newspaper Zycie.
Under Polish law, anyone offending religious sensibilities could face up to two years in prison or a fine.
The cardinal's letter followed a vocal campaign by pro-church groups, which demanded that the poster be banned in the predominantly Roman Catholic country.
Right-wing youths have torn down and spattered Flynt posters around the country with paint.
A spokeswoman for Krakow's prosecution office, Malgorzata Wilkosz-Sliwa, said no decision had yet been taken on whether to open a case against the poster.
The controversial poster was rejected by the Motion Picture Association of America and became the subject of vocal protests in Italy, France, Germany and Switzerland.
It advertises a film about the life of American pornography publishing king, Larry Flynt. The film won the "Golden Bear" award for best picture at the 47th Berlin Film festival last month.
Directed by Milos Forman, it also been nominated for two Oscars.
A Church protest two years ago against a British film, "The Priest," which depicted a homosexual cleric, helped boost box-office receipts.
